video_title: This Rune Giant Deck is TOTALLY OVERPOWERED!!

rune-giant: clock 1:27 (t=88.3): the only confirmed Rune Giant of the game goes at tile [8, 0], behind his own king tower (elixir 9.0 -> 5.0, HUD slot plus deploy label score 1.0), with Mother Witch at [8, 10] and Minions at [1, 13] added over the next 15 s — a build-from-the-back beatdown placement, not a bridge drop.

clock 0:43 (t=132, commentary): a second one is called deliberately off-lane — "we can go for the Rune Giant off to the side cuz he might try to get a Golden Knight ability" — keeping the enchanted push out of a Golden Knight dash chain.

The whole video is the buff pitch, stated in the first 20 s: "Rune Giant has gotten a massive buff in the most recent balance changes, making it extremely powerful. And now everyone is just wanting to use the Rune Giant. Rune Giant has actually become so popular on ladder" (t=8-21).

He values her purely for the enchant, never for her own damage: "Everything paired up with the Rune Giant is just so difficult to defend now. It just gets way way too much value and it just pairs up so nicely with the Hero Berserker" (t=26-35), and at t=141 "hopefully we can boost up the E-Barbs" as he plays Elite Barbarians next to her.

His own caveat at t=71-79: "That could have went very wrong if he either Vines earlier or if he just spammed that after the Berserker just got taken out."

bullets: Game 1 of a single-deck video (video t=4-169) built to show off the post-buff Rune Giant: "we are going to be playing the newly buffed Rune Giant... Rune Giant has gotten a massive buff in the most recent balance changes, making it extremely powerful" (t=6-14). Berserker is the Hero variant, confirmed on camera at t=35-37, and Zap is the Evolution (t=105-107).

Ryley names the core and admits the shape is odd: "it looks really strange because you don't really have what seems to be a win condition, but you just have so many strong cards in here that it is actually really hard to defend... just with just like Rune Giant, Berserker, E-Barbs, and Mother Witch" (t=80-92). He goes further at t=96-103: "whenever they are viable in the game, it does show that there is a little bit of a gap in the balancing at the moment because decks like these should really never work, to be honest."

First 90 s are pure defence in the left lane — Mother Witch at [2, 5] (clock 2:43), Berserker at [3, 9] and [3, 8] (2:36, 1:57), Elite Barbarians at [8, 9] (2:14), Zap at [2, 11] (2:04) — against an opponent Ryley reads as impatient: "this guy's just spamming the bridge every time he can" (t=55). Own left tower gives up 4858 -> 3549 HP over that stretch and nothing else.

The push only starts at clock 1:27: Rune Giant from the back at [8, 0], then Mother Witch at [8, 10], Minions at [1, 13] and a bridge Berserker at [3, 13] stacked on top, with Fireball + Evo Zap on the same tile [3, 19] clearing the Golden Knight answer (clock 1:10 and 1:08). The opponent's left tower goes 4858 -> 2897 -> 2472 -> 779, with the last ~1700 HP in the final 20 s.

Savage Survival is spent on defence, not offence: the ability at clock 1:53 clears a Battle Healer / Goblin / Spear Goblin stack — "because we had the ability, we still cleared out everything" (t=67) — and Ryley immediately flags the risk of not having it: "That could have went very wrong if he either Vines earlier" (t=71-75).

Closing summary in his own words at t=153-162: "The Mother Witch, the Berserkers, the E-Barbs, all with the Rune Giant is just so hard to stop. And then you pair that up with a nice Heal Spirit jump, dude, and there is nothing that your opponent can do." Result: win ("Very nice win to start off the video", t=163).

Deck-list caveat: the video-level consensus printed by the pipeline lists Skeletons in the eighth slot, but Fireball is deploy-label confirmed and named at t=103, and Skeletons appears in no per-game read. See the match file's Data gaps for the full override list (hand confidence 0.562).

new_deck.rationale: The Rune Giant is played from behind the king tower at clock 1:27 and everything else is stacked on top of her for one escalating push, which is beatdown shape — but the support cards (Berserker, Elite Barbarians, Mother Witch) are also dropped straight at the bridge for tempo, which is why bridge-spam is the secondary.
new_deck.why_it_works_md: A 3.25-elixir list with no conventional win condition — Ryley says so himself: "you don't really have what seems to be a win condition, but you just have so many strong cards in here that it is actually really hard to defend." The Rune Giant is a 4-elixir tank whose enchant adds bonus damage on every third attack, so the deck is built out of fast attackers that convert that buff: the Hero Berserker (0.6 s hit speed) and Elite Barbarians, with Mother Witch turning the cheap swarm the opponent throws at the push into Cursed Hogs. Because the tank is only 4 elixir, the deck can defend cheaply for a minute and a half and still afford a full push in double or triple elixir; Heal Spirit keeps the Mother Witch and Berserker alive through the spell chip, and Fireball plus Evolution Zap stacked on one tile clears the ranged answer. Its weak point, which Ryley names in this game, is the Berserker's 3-elixir Savage Survival: spend it early and a follow-up Vines or a swarm spam gets through with nothing left to hold.
